sectors.name: Technology
themes: Indonesia's digital economy penetration remains below 50%, driving sustained structural growth for local tech platforms and e-commerce enablers despite global tech volatility.
Government push for domestic data sovereignty and cloud adoption creates durable demand for local IT infrastructure and software services firms, insulating them from US rate cycles.
Rupiah stability and falling BI rate expectations are unlocking retail participation in small/mid-cap tech, amplifying liquidity-driven rallies in names like INET and DMMX.
sectors.ai: Buy pullbacks in Indonesian tech leaders (INET, ELIT, DMMX) as local outperformance (+2.90%) vs US (+0.72%) confirms domestic liquidity rotation into high-beta names. Signal WATCH suggests momentum is intact but not overbought; add on any 5-7% dip. Avoid chasing ASGR/NINE at current levels—profit-taking risk high after double-digit spikes. Focus on names with earnings visibility, not pure thematic plays.

sectors.name: Renewables & Climate-Tech
themes: Indonesia's mandatory biodiesel B40 and upcoming B50 mandate structurally lifts demand for palm-oil-based energy, benefiting integrated producers like TOBA and TPIA through feedstock-to-fuel verticals
The government's push for domestic EV battery and component manufacturing, tied to nickel downstreaming, creates durable earnings visibility for VKTR and CDIA as local content requirements tighten.
US solar demand recovery, driven by easing interest rates and IRA clarity, is transmitting upside to Indonesian climate-tech names via global supply-chain linkages, as seen in SEDG's jump.
sectors.ai: Indonesia's renewables rally is broadening beyond pure-play names into diversified conglomerates (BRPT, TPIA) and EV-linked operators (VKTR, CDIA), signaling institutional rotation into the country's energy-transition complex. Buy pullbacks in TOBA and VKTR on volume confirmation; trim POWR into strength as its run looks extended. The US solar recovery (SEDG) adds tailwind for local component makers.

sectors.name: Consumer & FMCG
themes: Lebaran-driven festive demand is a durable catalyst, lifting staples, snacks, and apparel volumes through Q1 2025 as retailers front-load inventory.
Indonesia's resilient middle-class spending, supported by stable inflation and minimum wage hikes, sustains premiumization in FMCG categories.
Supply-chain localization and digital distribution (e-commerce, social commerce) are structurally lowering costs and expanding reach for agile mid-cap consumer names.
sectors.ai: Buy selective momentum names (BIKE, CBUT, POLU) on domestic consumption strength ahead of Lebaran restocking; trim laggards as US softness drags sentiment. Rotate into mid-cap FMCG with pricing power and distribution expansion, targeting 2-3 week horizon for 15-25% upside.
